correctness.rationale: For odd-degree f in F_2[x], standard Artin–Schreier theory gives genus (deg f−1)/2 and a unique ramified rational point at infinity. Degree-six points above finite places arise from either a degree-six place with absolute trace Tr_6(f(a))=0 or a degree-three place with Tr_3(f(a))=1. Independently reconstructed F_64 using t^6+t+1, all nine exact degree-six and two degree-three Frobenius orbits. On the seven degree-six representatives 3,6,7,32,33,34,40 the sum of trace(a^j) vanishes for each j=0..20, but seven required inert traces would sum to one, impossible for any polynomial of degree ≤20. The degree-21 polynomial x^21+x^7 has all nine degree-six traces one and both degree-three traces zero; independent extension point counts N_1,N_2,N_3,N_6=(5,5,17,17) imply B_6=(N_6−N_3−N_2+N_1)/6=0. Both infinite-genus exclusion and witness follow from explicit finite-field identities plus genus/splitting theory; no claim for arbitrary curves.
